title: QBR - Celestia Cloud Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check covering usage trends, cost spikes, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Discussed options for Dedicated vs Hosted, proposed cost-optimization recommendations (batching, quantization), and agreed on benchmarks for POC. Action: Redwood to send cost breakdown, performance runbook, and schedule architecture deep-dive with infra team.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 min | Attendees: Maya, Arjun - Redwood; Lena, Samir, Diane - Celestia
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we should be recording this this is the QBR for Celestia, we'll do a quick agenda cover usage, costs, reliability incidents since last QBR, and then a roadmap alignment.
[00:15] Lena: great thanks maya. quick note Samir is dialed in from, uh, our SFO office, so might be on a slightly different line.
[00:22] Arjun: hey all, arjun here, i'll be covering the infra bits and the suggestions for batching / quantization.
[00:30] Samir: thanks, let's kick off.
[00:35] Maya: first slide, usage trend — you ramped tokens by about 80% q/q, looks like a lot of growth in embeddings for search autosuggest and rerank. is that accurate?
[00:48] Lena: yeah it's accurate, we've embedded more user content since jan, and search rerank volume spiked after the product launch. some of that is high-volume nightly jobs too.
[00:58] Samir: also we enabled longer context for a subset of requests, so avg token length increased. that hit cost too.
[01:10] Arjun: right, increased sequence length often changes kernel selection, which can spike vram and slow down throughput — we saw this in your metrics, there were a couple of pumps on p99 latency around march 8.
[01:25] Lena: about those p99 incidents, can you summarize root cause? we saw timeouts on a few user-facing endpoints.
[01:32] Arjun: yeah, the incidents were twofold: one was a sudden shift in sequence length distribution which led to suboptimal kernel path, and second we hit a cache miss storm because the prefix cache keys changed after a model variant update. transcription note: sometimes the call log says 'kay vee cache' which is actually KV cache.
[01:50] Diane: we also noticed higher error rate when the traffic hit the eu-west region, any region-specific notes?
[01:58] Maya: good catch, Diane. for eu-west we had an autoscaler cooldown misconfig which delayed additional Dedicated capacity spin-up; that's a config we recommended updating in march.
[02:12] Samir: is that an argument for moving more to Dedicated pools? we want predictability.
[02:18] Arjun: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, but comes with commit cost — there are middle options, like reserved burst capacity and overflow to hosted for spiky traffic.
[02:30] Lena: budget is a concern. can you share a cost breakdown by feature? last month our bill doubled yikes.
[02:38] Maya: yes, we'll share the cost breakdown. preliminary findings: embeddings for nightly indexing and long-context chat sessions are the major drivers. also model variant choice matters — the 70B quantized variant reduced cost per token but the latency profile changed.
[02:55] Samir: curious on the quantization note — you mentioned 4-bit that actually saved tokens? or saved compute?
[03:02] Arjun: quantization reduces memory and allows higher batch sizes; it lowers GPU hours, so compute cost is down but p95 latency can go up slightly depending on kernel and sequence length. we recommended a per-route quantization profile to balance cost and latency.
[03:20] Lena: can we see a simulation of cost if we switched nightly batch jobs to a different model or quantization?
[03:27] Maya: yes, next steps we'll run a cost simulation and a perf run: two scenarios — keep hosted with route-level quantization + smarter batching, or move nightly jobs to Dedicated reserved pool.
[03:42] Diane: for the Dedicated option, what is the minimum commit and expected savings?
[03:48] Maya: ballpark: a 6-12 month commit on a small Dedicated pool could reduce per-token compute cost by ~25-35% for steady workloads. exact #s we'll send in the spreadsheet.
[03:58] Samir: ok good. back to reliability: we had an incident on march 8, were there any mitigation recommendations so we don't see similar timeouts?
[04:06] Arjun: yes — two mitigations: 1) enforce a model pinning policy during rollouts to prevent silent variant switches; 2) adjust autoscaler cooldown and add capacity warm pools for eu-west; 3) enable prefix/KV caching for long-context templates to reduce repeated compute. note: logs sometimes show 'prefix cache collisions' due to truncated keys — we should hash keys consistently.
[04:32] Lena: about model pinning, how do we handle canary vs full rollout? we can't afford user-facing regressions.
[04:39] Maya: Redwood supports canary rollouts with traffic split, and auto-fallback policies if latency or error rates exceed thresholds. we can propose a rollout plan as part of the runbook.
[04:50] Samir: will that integrate with our SSO & audit requirements? we need to show change approvals.
[04:56] Maya: yes, audit logs and role-based access controls are captured in the Private offering; for Hosted we provide detailed request logs and enterprise audit exports. we'll include the audit log sample in the security pack.
[05:08] Diane: we also need SOC2 and ISO attestation docs.
[05:12] Maya: we'll share the latest SOC2 report and the compliance packet.
[05:16] Lena: thanks. shifting to roadmap — we wanted visibility into new Redwood features that might impact us in the next quarter.
[05:24] Arjun: upcoming work: 1) improved kernel selector heuristics for variable sequence lengths, 2) better autoscaling warm pools, 3) per-route quantization profiles in console, and 4) cost-optimizer suggestions for batching rules exposed via policy. target windows: rolling out between may and july.
[05:46] Samir: that kernel selector work sounds promising. can you share what metrics you'll expose so our SREs can monitor?
[05:53] Arjun: we'll expose per-model sequence-length histogram, p50/p95/p99 latency by sequence bucket, and kernel path telemetry so you can correlate changes.
[06:05] Lena: great. any blockers we should be aware of before we run the perf tests?
[06:10] Arjun: just two things: need a dedicated test account with representative traffic and sample prompts. also need permission to run sustained throughput tests that will consume tokens and compute.
[06:20] Maya: we'll send instructions and a test plan.
[06:25] Samir: timeline — we want the perf run in the next three weeks to decide on the Dedicated commit. can we do that?
[06:31] Maya: yes, if you provide traffic samples and agree to the test window we'll schedule a bench run.
[06:36] Diane: on security, our compliance team requested KMS integration and customer-managed keys for private data. is that available?
[06:42] Maya: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key; for Hosted there's envelope encryption and a KMS integration option for enterprise customers. we'll include configuration examples.
[06:55] Lena: ok sounds good. Any competitive concerns? we sometimes get questions from procurement comparing Redwood to Anthropic/Bedrock.
[07:03] Maya: competitors mentioned: Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock — difference we're emphasizing is production-focused tooling, deterministic rollouts and cost controls.
[07:14] Samir: procurement asked about price parity — they'll want the cost simulation.
[07:19] Maya: we'll include that in the spreadsheet.
[07:22] Arjun: small technical nit — when you hit p99s, include model variant id, token length, and worker kernel id in the alert payload so we can triage faster.
[07:33] Samir: good call.
[07:35] -- 10 minute marker --
[07:36] Maya: moving to action items and next steps.
[07:40] Maya: action 1: Redwood to send cost breakdown & simulation spreadsheet and QBR deck by 2026-04-27.
[07:47] Maya: action 2: Arjun to schedule infra deep-dive and perf run; needs traffic samples from Celestia; target perf run week of 2026-05-11.
[07:56] Maya: action 3: Redwood to share SOC2 + compliance packet and KMS integration guide by 2026-04-25.
[08:04] Lena: we'll get the traffic samples to Arjun by 2026-04-29.
[08:09] Diane: procurement will expect an SOW once we pick Dedicated option, can you start a draft?
[08:13] Maya: yes we can start a draft SOW, we'll flag optional Dedicated commit tiers.
[08:18] Samir: also follow-up on autoscaler cooldown config — Samir to test the recommended settings in staging and report back.
[08:25] Arjun: noted.
[08:28] Maya: ok we should recap quick. next steps: cost sim, perf run, compliance docs, SOW draft. any other items?
[08:36] Lena: none from me, thanks for the thorough review.
[08:39] Diane: thanks everyone.
[08:41] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and schedule the perf run. meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: some names and acronyms were mis-transcribed (kay vee cache -> KV cache), occasional filler words and overlap present.
